items.corrections: Original empirical factor compilation and multiple-testing analysis addresses part of the asset-pricing puzzle; no single theory resolves all named anomalies.
An IMF indicator predicts elevated crisis probabilities in a historical 108-economy panel; no deterministic causal framework predicts every crisis with policy lead time.
A Bank of Canada literature review explicitly documents large uncertainty and disagreement in neutral-rate estimates; this supports the unresolved estimation challenge, not a solved rate puzzle.
IMF proposes contractual reforms to address restructuring coordination problems. Proposal and facilitation goals do not establish achieved sovereign-debt crisis resolution.
FCA event analysis and the actual SEC/CFTC crash report provide bounded empirical microstructure evidence; universal crash prediction/prevention is unverified.
Primary six-agency ESG analysis decomposes rating disagreement; measurement taxonomy does not establish causal financial or environmental impact.

IMF balance-sheet and agent-based modeling explains loan/deposit creation with liquidity constraints in its specified monetary framework. No complete universal monetary-financial theory is demonstrated.
Behavioral-finance review explicitly calls for further theory/testing and social-finance work; it does not present a settled unified predictive theory.
A two-year local bird-conservation funding experiment raised over $16,000 and found strategic/framing effects. It does not establish universal global ecosystem-service valuation and finance.

Primary papers model capital/risk constraints and empirically assess transaction-cost explanations for return predictability. They do not derive an exact universal information-theoretic arbitrage bound.
